_scope: CALIBRATED FOR 5001-TIF-7-1C AND 5001-TIF-CC-1C — the two share one die, one press template and one imposition; only the canvas colour differs, and that is a proof colour, not a geometry.
_template_file: 5001-TIF-7-1C.pdf and 5001-TIF-CC-1C.pdf — two vendor files, one geometry
_measured_by: content-stream rectangles on the guide page; magenta imprint crosshairs on the press sheet
_shared_spec_evidence: The vendor's two templates were compared rather than assumed equal: every large rectangle on the guide page matches to a tenth of a point, and both crosshairs to a hundredth. They differ only in the item number printed in the title, which is why each product keeps its own template file and they share this one spec.
_unverified: Derived by measurement, never checked against a printed sheet. Two things to confirm at press before a live job: that the art lands on the crosshairs, and that ROTATED_SIDE1_DIR turns the bag the right way up.
_geometry_note: The die is 1043.9 x 2232.0 pt (14.50" x 31.00") — the whole flat body, both panels, hinged at the fold on y=1230.3. Each panel is therefore 15.50" tall. The press sheet's panel band is 1044 pt tall, which is the die WIDTH to within a tenth of a point, and 15.50" does not fit in 14.50": the panel is imposed rotated 90°. That equality is the measurement this whole layout rests on.
_zone_note: The zone below is the imprint area the configurator offers, which is the purple body outline the customer was told they could print up to — not the template's cyan 'Maximum Imprint Area' rectangle, which is 883.5 x 801.9 pt (12.27" x 11.14"). Proof and press both use the configurator's zone so the three agree; the cyan rectangle printed on the guide page will read smaller than the art placed over it. Both rectangles share a centre, so nothing shifts — only the size differs.
_positions_note: Both centres read straight off the magenta crosshairs the vendor drew at the dead centre of each imprint — no arc-fitting or inference. Measured at 150 dpi and agreeing with the sheet's own 1044 pt band pitch to 0.4 pt. 'vertical': false is what turns the art 90°.
_proof_cover_note: Covers the step-1/step-2 notes, the colour legend and the ART REQUIREMENTS box — all of which describe guide furniture this proof no longer shows. Stops below the product photo and its 'Front' caption, which stay: they tell the customer which panel they are looking at. The ART REQUIREMENTS box is outlined vector, not live text, so it was measured off a render rather than from pdftotext.
_info_panel_note: Sits in the column the cover rectangle just cleared. The koozie defaults are for an 1152 x 1656 page; this one is 2215 x 2809, so the block is placed and scaled for it rather than inherited.
_flat_proof_note: The 1-side This Is Fast job prints the front only, but the bag still has a back — so the flat proof shows both panels with the back blank, the back turned upright the way the koozies turn theirs, and simplified handle tabs on each.
_die_fill_note: The whole flat body as one rectangle — this die has no handle cut-outs, so a rectangle is the die, not an approximation of it. Painted by the overlay rather than by fill_die_cut because this template strokes its die near the start of the content stream and its own panel blocks paint over anything filled in place.
_die_note: Panel 1 is the front (printed), panel 2 the back, hinged at the fold on y=1230.3. The 1-side This Is Fast process prints the front only; the back is greyed out on the template.
